_comment: The regcf subject sidecar. Everything the pipeline needs to know about
THIS body of law lives here; everything about the pipeline itself lives in
etc/go/. Validated by etc/go/lib/subject.mjs, which refuses unknown keys
and missing files. Free-prose idiosyncrasies live in NOTES.md, which no
script reads. All paths are repo-root-relative.
The three sections below are named for WHAT THEY ARE, not for which pass
produced them (ruling R2/R3). 'natlang_sources' is the fetched legal text and
the sweep's findings; 'comparison' holds the declarations that exist only to
relate two encodings; 'encodings' holds ADDITIONAL encodings of the same law,
keyed by an id that names the OCCASION ('cleanroom-2026-08'), never its
position in a sequence. Their paths' EXISTENCE is optional: producing them is
agent work, and the stages report SKIPPED with a named reason until they
appear. An additional encoding's modules may not name a committed module --
SPEC.md section 8's diff compares the two, so an additional module that IS the
committed one makes that comparison an identity.
An additional encoding's 'checks' floors measure THAT ENCODING, never the
committed one. min_assertions 39 = assertions_total from 'l4 run
--json' results[] over regcf-denovo.l4, the figure p6-tests compares against
(the source text carries 40 '#ASSERT' strings; the 40th is prose in a
comment at regcf-denovo.l4:3590). min_dated_arms 0 = the population under
p3-check's matcher: the module routes rule-date logic through a helper
abstraction over YMD constants, which that matcher cannot see -- NOTES.md
has the census. A 0 floor makes p3-check report the sub-check NOT CHECKED
rather than vacuously green.
